knowledge:
- key_parameters: normalise_by_factor=used to normalize HTSeq counts by library size ;; extract_features=supports "human" or "mouse" via the organism parameter, and allows custom common_features, GO_terms, and extra_genes ;; assess_cell_quality_PCA=the file parameter specifies the path to write the diagnostic PCA plot PDF ;; assess_cell_quality_SVM=requires training_features, training_labels, param (hyperparameters), and test_features to perform ensemble classification
- alternatives: PCA-based outlier detection (assess_cell_quality_PCA) is unsupervised and useful when no training data is available, but is less successful at detecting multiples. SVM-based classification (assess_cell_quality_SVM) is supervised, more accurate, and handles multiples better, but requires matching training data or using "common" features which have less power.
- when_to_use: When performing quality control on single-cell RNA-seq datasets (specifically mouse or human) to identify and filter out low-quality or deceptive cells before downstream analysis.
- pitfalls: Counts from Cufflinks must be transformed from FPKM to TPM before feature extraction ;; Non-mouse/human organisms require manual database installation (e.g. org.Hs.eg.db) and correct gene ID mapping ;; Missing features in the output matrix indicate they all had the same value (e.g., zero ERCC reads) ;; The classifier detects "deceptive" low-quality cells not visible under a microscope, which may lead to higher filtering rates than expected from visual inspection.

workflows.name: pca_based_quality_assessment
workflows.intent: Identify low-quality cells using unsupervised PCA-based outlier detection on extracted biological and technical features.
input: gene_counts.tsv (Gene expression matrix, Genes x Cells)
read_stats.tsv (Read statistics matrix, Cells x Metrics, e.g. from celloline)
workflows.stages: 1. Normalize gene expression counts using normalise_by_factor ;; 2. Extract biological and technical features using extract_features ;; 3. Assess cell quality and detect outliers using assess_cell_quality_PCA
workflows.code:
sample_counts_nm <- normalise_by_factor(sample_counts, colSums(sample_counts))
sample_features <- extract_features(sample_counts_nm, sample_stats)
sample_features_all <- sample_features[[1]]
sample_qual_pca <- assess_cell_quality_PCA(sample_features_all)
training_quality_PCA_allF <- assess_cell_quality_PCA(
  training_mES_features_all, file = "./training_quality_PCA_allF.pdf")

workflows.name: svm_based_quality_classification
workflows.intent: Classify low-quality cells using a supervised SVM ensemble model trained on reference datasets.
input: gene_counts.tsv (Gene expression matrix, Genes x Cells)
read_stats.tsv (Read statistics matrix, Cells x Metrics, e.g. from celloline)
workflows.stages: 1. Normalize gene expression counts using normalise_by_factor ;; 2. Extract biological and technical features using extract_features ;; 3. Classify cell quality using assess_cell_quality_SVM with training features, training labels, and optimized hyperparameters
workflows.code:
sample_counts_nm <- normalise_by_factor(sample_counts, colSums(sample_counts))
sample_features <- extract_features(sample_counts_nm, sample_stats)
mES1_features_all <- mES1_features[[1]]
mES1_quality_SVM <- assess_cell_quality_SVM(
  training_mES_features_all, training_mES_labels[,2], param_mES_all, 
  mES1_features_all)
